findings.message: Bed probe 'bed_probe': a unit at the short end of its spread (switching distance 4 mm on steel (BTT Eddy manual (vendor_docs/BTT_Eddy_Series_User_Manual_20250507.pdf) 4.1: mounted 2-3 mm above the tip, coil current calibrated at 20 mm, so it reads over at least 2-20 mm; Klipper probe_eddy_current triggers at the height PROBE_EDDY_CURRENT_CALIBRATE sets: 4 mm is a setting inside that range), +/-10% unit to unit (from its ratings)) switches with the nozzle 1.10 mm above the bed as drawn. The toolhead's stack-up between face and tip (0.95 mm, 99.7 %) and the bed's flatness over the 37.02 mm between them (0.23 mm) add up to 1.19 mm: with the face that much too high, or the bed that much higher under the nozzle, the nozzle touches first.

data.hint: Lower the face (it may come down to 1.19 mm above the tip), use a sensor with more range on this bed, or set the sensor's height on the built machine with its nuts against a gauge and say so in the build instructions (that removes the stack-up, not the bed's flatness).

findings.message: Bed probe 'bed_probe' is offset (-8, 36.146) mm from the nozzle and kept 15.3 mm inside the plate edge, so strips of the print area are never probed: {'x_high': 8.0, 'y_low': np.float64(36.15), 'y_high': np.float64(9.35)} (mm wide; print area declared: design.printer['print_area'] = 186.6 x 208.1 mm, centred on the plate). The firmware holds the nearest measured value there.

data.hint: Acceptable if the bed is flat at the edges; otherwise move the probe closer to the nozzle or shrink the print area.

findings.message: Probe 'bed_probe' is rated for 60 degC ambient (BTT Eddy manual (vendor_docs/BTT_Eddy_Series_User_Manual_20250507.pdf) 1: operating temperature <= 60 degC ambient). Its face works 2.7 mm above a bed that runs up to 80 degC: the sensor is estimated at 36.9 to 58.4 degC (moving in room air to parked over the bed), and the high end is within the 10 K asked of an unvalidated estimate (margin 1.6 K).

data.hint: Lower the bed's highest target, use a sensor rated for a higher ambient, or keep the probe off the bed except while probing and probe at one fixed bed temperature.

findings.message: Heater 'extruder': a shorted MOSFET is survived only because the firmware drops the supply relay (peak 282 degC). There is no cut-off that works if the controller has also hung.
Loom 'gantry': the straight line between its two clamps passes through 'leadscrew_fl' at pose {'y': 93.6}; the free loop has to bend round it and may rub.

The only assembly order found installs something before the part that supports it (around ['beam_bolt_left', 'beam_bolt_left_1', 'beam_bolt_left_1_tnut', 'beam_bolt_left_1_washer', 'beam_bolt_left_1_washer_2', 'beam_bolt_left_tnut']); it would need holding in place.

data.hint: Add a locating feature, change which part carries the screws, or put the parts in one bench sub-assembly.

findings.message: A 1 kg print at the worst corner of the print area lowers the print surface there by 0.030 mm (bonded joints 0.029, screw-only joints 0.030; of which guides and nut 0.001), more than 0.1 of a 0.2 mm layer (0.020 mm). The bed is levelled and meshed empty, so neither sees it.

data.hint: Shorten the overhang, space the guide blocks further apart along the rail, stiffen the arms, or support the bed at a second or third point.

findings.message: Guide moment checks use the home pose and bounding-box centres of mass; treat them as estimates.

40 off-the-shelf part type(s) still use typical class values, not vendor data: BHCS-FL-M5x10, BRG-608, CAM-RPI-CM3-SC1223, CONTACTOR-FINDER-22.32.0.120.4320, CTRL-OCTOPUS-V1.1, DIN-ENDSTOP-WAGO-249-117, DIN-RAIL-WAGO-210-112-246, DIN-RAIL-WAGO-210-112-47, ENDSTOP-OMRON-D2F-01L, ESTOP-OMRON-A22E-M-02, EXT2020-230, EXT2020-276 and 28 more. Confirm against the chosen vendor's datasheet (59 part type(s) are vendor-backed; see docs/VENDOR_DATA.md).

Joint z has 1.65 mm of declared over-travel past the nozzle plane: the bed meeting the nozzle tip there was not counted as a collision (checked to 1.65 mm past). 1 part(s) on the nozzle's body (hotend) ride with the nozzle and were checked with the bed at nozzle contact plus their toolhead margin; every other pair was checked over the whole over-travel. The probe's face height and trigger margin are judged by the subsystems verifier.
2 elements are commodity parts with no single vendor part number fixed: ['x_endstop', 'y_endstop']. Their ratings are class values (see sources); fix a vendor part before purchase.
Cold-start inrush of psu is 60.0 A (data sheet, typical): the T8A time-lag fuse is assumed to ride through it; I2t was not checked.

Not modelled: EMC and noise coupling, firmware bugs, crimp and solder quality, connector wear, real PID autotune on the real heater, heater tolerance (+/-10 %), mains transients. See docs/ELECTRICAL.md.
nut_thrust: raw peak 13.09 MPa is at the fixed boundary (artificially stiff clamp); governing stress taken away from it.
nut_thrust: FoS 32.8 is far above the 3.0 target; mass could be removed.
x_belt_pull: raw peak 17.85 MPa is at the fixed boundary (artificially stiff clamp); governing stress taken away from it.
bed_self_weight_sag: raw peak 2.23 MPa is at the fixed boundary (artificially stiff clamp); governing stress taken away from it.
bed_self_weight_sag: FoS 129.6 is far above the 3.0 target; mass could be removed.

Joint z: one screw may stand 1.46 mm out of the plane of the others (1.44 mm across the print area) before the first limit is reached (z_carriage_rear: static moment and load / 3, z_nut_fl); every nut stays seated up to 0.43 mm. The routine height error (LSC-015 budget) is 0.142 mm.

G9SE input loop: A22E-M-02 NC contacts (two channels) + spare pair 1: door interlock (future) + spare pair 2: smoke / heat detector (future); manual reset button on T33/T34. The GPIO path can only drop the contactor; after an e-stop, power returns only through the G9SE's manual reset. Heater runaway when the Pi or Klipper hangs: the Octopus's MCU turns its heater outputs off by itself when the host stops refreshing them (Klipper max_duration) and shuts down; the bed also has its CS712025Y thermostat (120 degC). If the MCU itself hangs with a heater on, or a MOSFET fails shorted, nothing automatic cuts the hotend (the Revo PTC self-limits near 420 degC in the model) until the e-stop is pressed or the future smoke / heat contact opens the loop. The e-stop is on the front-left post (head forward, 35 mm proud); the G9SE is outside the back wall (z 283-407, inside the spool's footprint): its 111.6 mm depth cannot stand in the bay under the carrier (which comes down to z 142)

parts.name: carriage_plate_left
parts.desc: Carriage plate (left): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_left (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

findings.message: carriage_plate_left (al6061, 1.6 mm, flat): assigned SendCutSend: passes. Passes the published rules of: Fictiv, Hubs (Protolabs Network), OSH Cut, Protolabs, SendCutSend, Xometry.

parts.name: carriage_plate_right
parts.desc: Carriage plate (right): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_right (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

findings.message: carriage_plate_right (al6061, 1.6 mm, flat): assigned SendCutSend: passes. Passes the published rules of: Fictiv, Hubs (Protolabs Network), OSH Cut, Protolabs, SendCutSend, Xometry.

parts.name: carriage_plate_rear
parts.desc: Carriage plate (rear): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_rear (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: nut_plate
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_rear (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 56.2 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

parts.name: nut_plate_fl
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut_fl (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew_fl. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_left (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 9.1 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin_fl (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper_fl, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

findings.message: y_plate_right: 6 hole(s) or cut-out(s) narrower than the 4.75 mm sheet (smallest 3.50 mm at [150.0, -51.61, 419.38]): they cut, but taper and lose accuracy.
findings.hint: Make them at least 4.75 mm, or drill or ream them after cutting if the size matters.

findings.message: y_plate_right: 3 hole(s) with less than 4.75 mm of material to the edge (least 3.35 mm at [180.22, -27.87, 419.38]): the web overheats and distorts, and tears if the part is bent or loaded.
findings.hint: Move the hole in, or widen the part there, to leave at least 4.75 mm.

findings.message: y_plate_right: 2 pair(s) of holes or cut-outs with too little material between them (least 4.02 mm at [175.11, -50.14, 419.38], wanted 4.75 mm = 1 x thickness).
findings.hint: Space them out, or merge them into one cut-out.

findings.message: y_plate_right: SendCutSend rule sendcutsend.cut.hole_min_al6061_page: smallest hole or cut-out 3.5 mm (6 of 12), limit >= 4.75 mm (warning: the supplier's words: "Design holes no smaller than material thickness.").

y_plate_right: SendCutSend rule sendcutsend.cut.hole_edge_al6061_page: hole edge to part edge 3.75 mm (1 of 4), limit >= 7.12 mm (warning: the supplier's words: "Keep holes and cutouts 1.5–2× material thickness away from edges to prevent warping or distortion.").

y_plate_right: SendCutSend rule sendcutsend.cut.slot_edge_w_ratio: slot to edge or next feature 3.35 mm (4 of 6), limit >= 7.2 mm (warning: the supplier's words: "we generally recommend keeping your holes at least 1X their diameter from an edge and slots at least 1.5X their width away from edges or other cut features.").
Belt y_belt: pulley y_idler is 1.35 mm from y_plate_right (pose {'y': -104.5, 'x': 94.8, 'z': 181.7}); under 2 mm a flange rubs the plate with the bearing's axial play or the hub's run-out (BLT-061).
findings.hint: Space the pulley off the plate (a thicker spacer or a second washer, moving the belt plane with it), or relieve the plate. Limit: design.practice['limits']['BLT-061.pulley_plate_clearance_mm'].

findings.message: y_plate_right (al6061, 4.75 mm, flat): assigned SendCutSend: passes, 3 recommendation(s) not met. Passes the published rules of: Fictiv, Hubs (Protolabs Network), OSH Cut, Protolabs, SendCutSend, Xometry.

findings.message: Bed probe 'bed_probe': a unit at the short end of its spread (switching distance 4 mm on steel (BTT Eddy manual (vendor_docs/BTT_Eddy_Series_User_Manual_20250507.pdf) 4.1: mounted 2-3 mm above the tip, coil current calibrated at 20 mm, so it reads over at least 2-20 mm; Klipper probe_eddy_current triggers at the height PROBE_EDDY_CURRENT_CALIBRATE sets: 4 mm is a setting inside that range), +/-10% unit to unit (from its ratings)) switches with the nozzle 1.10 mm above the bed as drawn. The toolhead's stack-up between face and tip (0.95 mm, 99.7 %) and the bed's flatness over the 37.02 mm between them (0.23 mm) add up to 1.19 mm: with the face that much too high, or the bed that much higher under the nozzle, the nozzle touches first.
findings.hint: Lower the face (it may come down to 1.19 mm above the tip), use a sensor with more range on this bed, or set the sensor's height on the built machine with its nuts against a gauge and say so in the build instructions (that removes the stack-up, not the bed's flatness).

findings.message: Bed probe 'bed_probe' is offset (-8, 36.146) mm from the nozzle and kept 15.3 mm inside the plate edge, so strips of the print area are never probed: {'x_high': 8.0, 'y_low': np.float64(36.15), 'y_high': np.float64(9.35)} (mm wide; print area declared: design.printer['print_area'] = 186.6 x 208.1 mm, centred on the plate). The firmware holds the nearest measured value there.
findings.hint: Acceptable if the bed is flat at the edges; otherwise move the probe closer to the nozzle or shrink the print area.

level_over_travel.from_screw_lead_error_note: one screw at its lead-accuracy limit over the 183 mm travel (0.061 mm; ASSUMED: +/-0.1 mm per 300 mm, the class figure for rolled trapezoidal screws (Elesa-Ganter and igus state it for their own screws, practice_refs/13_*; not for this T8 screw, whose maker gives none: set ratings['lead_accuracy_mm_per_300mm'] on the part when it is known))

screw_synchronisation.basis: one motor per screw: at power-up each motor settles on its nearest full-step detent, up to 2 full steps (2 mm lead / 200 x 2 = 0.02 mm) apart; lost steps add without limit until re-levelled
screw_synchronisation.how: one screw high by the height error, the bed on its supports' stiffness: part becomes tilt, part force (linear: every nut taken as seated; see nut_seating_and_lead_error for what happens when one is not)

nut_seating.reverse_gap_note: POM anti-backlash nut (no backlash: assumed) held with the keeper's 1 mm play (v12: stock 6 mm spacer over the 5 mm flange)

lead_accuracy.basis: ASSUMED: +/-0.1 mm per 300 mm, the class figure for rolled trapezoidal screws (Elesa-Ganter and igus state it for their own screws, practice_refs/13_*; not for this T8 screw, whose maker gives none: set ratings['lead_accuracy_mm_per_300mm'] on the part when it is known)

nut_seating_and_lead_error.bearing_axial_note: BRG-022: the largest nut load of any case above, all on one bearing, against 0.25 C0 (SKF: small bearings, bore up to about 12 mm)
nut_seating_and_lead_error.lead_error_note: per screw, at the class limit; the difference between two screws is between 0 (same error) and twice this (opposite limits). It grows with the distance moved from the height the bed was trammed at; neither a belt nor independent motors remove it (a firmware re-level corrects it only at the height it is run at)

levels.case: synchronisation + lead error over the travel, one screw at its class limit
synchronisation + lead error over the travel, two screws at opposite limits

nut_seating_and_lead_error.how: rigid body on guide springs and one-way nut springs (active-set contact); flexure of arms and plate is not in these figures; guide forces are those of the support model

tilt_allowance.nut_tilt_basis: keeper play 1 mm over the POM nut's 26 mm flange (drawing A4003)
tilt_allowance.how: one screw high by h, the others where they are; rigid body on guide blocks, mounts and nuts (every nut holding both ways); linear in h. Block limit: moments about the block's three axes and its force over their static ratings, added, on top of the moving mass's share. Web limit: bending and torsion of a declared flexure web. Not in it: the clearance of a ZF block (it would add free tilt), flexure of the carrier, screw bending, the firmware's own limits

# mains contactor ahead of the 24 V supply: switched from a host (Pi) GPIO by Moonraker, not by Klipper:

# input shaper: predicted by the twin, not measured: resonance X 73.3 Hz, Y 61.2 Hz (belt stiffness only, no FEA frame stiffness); damping assumed. Run SHAPER_CALIBRATE

[output_pin lights]

pwm: True

shutdown_value: 0

# Quarton VLM-520-56 line laser (Class 1M): off by default, on only inside the measurement macro; PN2222A from Pi GPIO17
[output_pin nozzle_laser]
pin: host:gpio17
value: 0
shutdown_value: 0

# commissioning (owner, v11.1 plan): probe only after the bed has soaked at temperature
[gcode_macro START_PRINT]
gcode:
    {% set BED = params.BED|default(60)|float %}
    {% set SOAK = params.SOAK|default(1831)|int %}
    M190 S{BED}
    G4 P{SOAK * 1000}
    G28
    Z_TILT_ADJUST
    BED_MESH_CALIBRATE
    # purge / prime line at the FRONT edge of the sheet (owner: the arm never needs the rear)
    G90
    G1 X5 Y1.5 Z5 F9000
    G1 Z0.3 F600
    G92 E0
    G1 X120 Y1.5 E18 F1500
    G1 X150 Y1.5 E20 F3000
    G1 Z2 F600

[gcode_macro LASER_CAPTURE]
gcode:
    SET_PIN PIN=lights VALUE=0.1
    SET_PIN PIN=nozzle_laser VALUE=1
    G4 P2000
    SET_PIN PIN=nozzle_laser VALUE=0
    SET_PIN PIN=lights VALUE=0.5

findings.message: Corners and seams bulge up to 0.40 mm (material keeps flowing while the nozzle slows; size depends on the 32 ms extruder lag (direct drive, 0.4 mm nozzle: factory pressure-advance values (fitted_parameters.json: extruder_lag_s), range 0.02 to 0.058 s) and on the firmware's pressure advance).
